title: 27yo F Ruptured Ectopic Pregnancy
chiefComplaint: Sudden lower abdominal pain and collapse
background: Sudden severe right lower quadrant pain two hours ago while at work, followed by a witnessed syncopal episode. She reports light vaginal spotting for three days and thought her period was late. Last menstrual period was seven weeks ago and she describes her cycles as usually regular. She has a copper intrauterine device inserted 18 months ago and a past episode of chlamydia treated three years ago. She has not taken a pregnancy test. Right shoulder tip pain started in the ambulance.

exam.finding: Pale, clammy, restless with pain, lying still with knees drawn up
Conjunctival pallor, dry mucous membranes, no jaundice, no lymphadenopathy
Sinus tachycardia, thready radial pulse, capillary refill 4 seconds, normal heart sounds, JVP not visible
Clear breath sounds, shallow rapid respirations limited by abdominal pain
Distended and diffusely tender with worst pain in the right iliac fossa, guarding and rebound tenderness, percussion tenderness across the lower abdomen, absent bowel sounds
Dark blood in the vaginal vault, closed cervical os, IUD threads visible, severe cervical motion tenderness, tender fullness in the right adnexa, boggy pouch of Douglas
Cool pale peripheries with mottling to the knees, no rash, no bruising
GCS 14 (E4V4M6), anxious and slow to respond during pain spikes, no focal deficit

investigations.name: Urine beta-hCG
investigations.report: Positive. Any woman of reproductive age with abdominal pain and shock has an ectopic pregnancy until proven otherwise, and an intrauterine device does not exclude pregnancy.

investigations.name: Bedside FAST and transvaginal ultrasound
investigations.report: Free fluid in Morison's pouch and the pelvis with echogenic swirling material suggesting clotted blood. Empty uterus with a thin endometrial stripe and the IUD in situ. Right adnexal heterogeneous mass 34 mm separate from the ovary with surrounding fluid. No intrauterine gestational sac.

investigations.name: Haemoglobin
investigations.report: Acute anaemia from intraperitoneal haemorrhage. A normal initial haemoglobin would not have excluded this.

investigations.name: Serum beta-hCG
investigations.report: Above the discriminatory zone. An empty uterus at this level with free fluid indicates ectopic pregnancy. In an unstable patient this result should not delay theatre.

investigations.name: Blood group and crossmatch
investigations.report: Rh negative. Four units crossmatched. Anti-D immunoglobulin required.

investigations.name: INR and fibrinogen
investigations.report: Early dilutional and consumptive coagulopathy. Give balanced blood product ratios rather than crystalloid.

data.label: Urine pregnancy test and two large bore IV lines with bloods
actions: CBC, coagulation, lactate, group and crossmatch 4 units

data.label: Bedside FAST and transvaginal ultrasound without leaving the resuscitation area
Activate massive transfusion and give blood, not litres of crystalloid

doseMap.Emergency O negative red cells: 2 units immediately while crossmatched blood is prepared
doseMap.Limited crystalloid: Keep under 1000 mL, permissive hypotension until bleeding is controlled

data.label: Transient response
data.narrative: Two units of packed cells lift her pressure briefly, then it starts falling again. This is a transient responder. The bleeding is surgical and no amount of product will fix it in the department.

data.label: Tell her she is pregnant and that the pregnancy cannot be saved, before she goes to theatre (Empathy)
data.narrative: You take 40 seconds to say she is pregnant, that the pregnancy is in the wrong place and cannot survive, and that surgery now is what will save her life. You ask if there is anyone she wants called. She asks you to call her sister. Doing this before anaesthesia rather than after is the difference between informed consent and a patient waking up to news nobody prepared her for.

data.label: Immediate obstetrics and gynaecology referral for theatre
actions: Nil by mouth and anaesthetic review
Consent for laparoscopy or laparotomy, possible salpingectomy

data.label: To theatre
data.narrative: She is in theatre 28 minutes after arrival. Laparoscopy finds 1200 mL of haemoperitoneum and a ruptured right tubal pregnancy. Right salpingectomy is performed and the bleeding stops.

data.label: Post-operative care including anti-D for this Rh negative patient
actions: Early pregnancy unit follow up and counselling

data.label: Disposition
data.narrative: Haemoglobin is 9.6 g/dL after four units. She is extubated and stable on the gynaecology ward. Counselling covers future fertility with one remaining tube and the raised risk of a repeat ectopic pregnancy. Her sister is at the bedside.
